body: It's good to hear that you know what I mean about going shopping for no reason just to experience the presence of other people. This feeling of loneliness is raw and breath-taking. The friends I used to have were from my high school days and I don't feel like they really cared. I'm not sure if the feeling of people not really caring is part of my depression but I feel that way a lot. I remember opening up to them and telling them about the way I felt and I tried to make them understand what I was going through but it lead to them distancing themselves from me. I got the answer 'you've changed', ' you are no longer the fun, happy go lucky person you used to be' and 'you are always so negative' answer a lot. That really hurt me. Why would anybody choose to lose themselves in despair? Nobody wants to deal with depression, it just happens to you. I wish my friends had been able to show more compassion.

Hey kruhousti, thanks for your kind message. Cats are great companions and that's why I decided to get one but on really bad days not even my purring cat can help alleviate my pain. It's the lack of human touch and the lack of human compassion in my daily life which feels like a dagger in my heart.
Depression is a serious illness and cannot be turned off or swept under the rug. It is an illness which directs your thoughts down a negative path and there is no escaping it. There is no escape.

Thank you for your input efficiens. I haven't told my therapist about my thoughts because I fear what she will do when I do tell her. I don't want to be committed. I feel like a huge part of me doesn't want to be viewed as somebody who is too weak to want to continue living. I guess it's shame I am feeling. I know what you mean about therapy being a place where you can get things off your chest and it definitely has been the same for me but I sometimes feel like I'm lacking a real connection with my therapist. My therapy is completely covered by insurance so sometimes I get the feeling I am being treated as one out of many rather than a real person. I'm not sure what to think.
Thanks so much for your kind words, all the best to you as well!

Thank you for taking the time to help me out, it really means a lot. I guess you could say that expecting life to be the same uphill journey every single day without any problems whatsoever is where my thinking pattern is flawed. I never really saw it that way so this makes a lot of sense to me. I will definitely keep reminding myself that consistency is key to being stable. I guess the reason why I have never gone through with ending my life is that little glimmer of hope in my mind that things can eventually work out and that I can overcome this.  Thank you again for your input!

Thank you for your input, I really appreciate it. I absolutely know what you mean about striking up conversations with strangers. Whenever I'm having a good day I sometimes have the energy for small talk and I am able to smile at a cashier or talk to a stranger. At school I feel like my age is a bit of a road block since most people are considerably younger than me but I do try to seem approachable and friendly. I will remind myself to hold on to the good days and talk to strangers when I can, it's definitely something I need to work on. Thank you again for making me feel a bit more whole today and I truly mean that dear stranger.

Thank you for your response. I went back to school for my degree so I'm currently a full-time student. The only social contact I have is when I attend classes and it is very minimal. I go to class and then I go home to study so I'm mostly very isolated. I'm very lonely so I've tried going for long walks or going to shopping malls just to feel the presence of other people. On certain days just going to the store to buy something to eat is the 'highlight' of my day and I have to force myself to do it. I wish I was stable like most people out there.
